title: Model Routing Becomes the Frontier AI Control Plane
description: Today’s Six-Month Signal covers Anthropic Sonnet 5 and Fable/Mythos access, GitHub Copilot’s model-routing and budget controls, Fullstack Code Arena, Google ADK and Genkit agent workflows, Latent Space’s skill-engineering interview with Paul Bakaus, and inference-economics analysis from Training Data with Dylan Patel, Air Street, and SemiAnalysis. The through-line: frontier AI is becoming a managed execution environment, not just a leaderboard race.

title: Governed AI Becomes the Frontier Stack
description: Today's episode argues that the next six months of AI systems will be shaped less by raw leaderboard gains and more by governed execution: Anthropic's Fable 5 safeguards, Arena's Fullstack Code Arena, Artificial Analysis and Vals task-economics data, and Cognition/LangChain workflow launches. Sources include Anthropic, Arena, Artificial Analysis, Vals AI, Cognition, LangChain, Simon Willison, SemiAnalysis, Google, and The Information.

title: AI Becomes an Industrial System
description: Today’s episode tracks five signals for the six-month AI frontier: Import AI on Fable’s KernelBench-Mega result, Armin Ronacher and Simon Willison on tool-call regressions, LiteLLM/LangChain/Vercel release notes on the agent control plane, Software Synthesis on modular post-training, and The Cognitive Revolution’s Liquid AI interview on device-native models. The through-line is that frontier AI is becoming an industrial system: kernels, tool contracts, control planes, adaptations, and deployment topology now matter as much as model rankings.

title: Guardrails Become the Agent Frontier
description: Today's Six-Month Signal leads with Artificial Analysis' AutomationBench-AA, which reframes SaaS-agent progress around guardrail-adjusted task completion and per-task economics. The episode also covers OpenAI's GPT-Realtime-2.1 voice-agent release, Tencent's Hy3 open MoE model, and reporting from Import AI, Simon Willison, and Every on Fable as both an AI R&D automator and workflow debugger.

title: Agents Become Measurable, Governed, and Routable
description: Today’s episode leads on Artificial Analysis and Zapier’s AutomationBench-AA, which turns real SaaS workflow completion into a guardrail-adjusted cost benchmark. It also covers The Information’s GPT-5.6 release-governance reporting, ARC Prize’s first ARC-AGI-3 milestone, Anthropic’s Claude Code product narrative, and Tencent Hy3 as a deployability signal for open models.

title: Feedback Ownership Becomes the Frontier AI Advantage
description: Today’s episode tracks why the six-month AI frontier is shifting from raw model scale to ownership of verified workflow feedback. Sources include Cursor and Artificial Analysis on Grok 4.5, Every on GPT-5.6 Sol, Epoch AI on EBR-bench, LangChain/NVIDIA on governed agent infrastructure, and The Information on enterprise SaaS consolidation.

title: Governed Work Loops Become the Frontier AI Runtime
description: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 release, ChatGPT Work, and new runtime primitives point to frontier AI becoming a governed work environment rather than just a model leaderboard. This episode also covers Artificial Analysis' EnterpriseOps-Gym-AA benchmark, Every's GPT-5.6 knowledge-work loop essay, METR's Anthropic researcher-uplift note, and Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 pricing response.

title: The Six-Month Signal — Human Judgment Becomes System Architecture
description: Automated evals recover 87% of known failures, a small agent harness turns bug triage into bounded work, and Davidad explains why his AI-catastrophe forecast has fallen below 5%.

title: The Six-Month Signal — Measured Work
description: Three signals for the next six months: task-level agent economics, process-supervised specialist models, and action-conditioned world models.

title: The Six-Month Signal — Attack, Truth, and Orchestration
description: Four signals for the next six months: automated adversarial training, tool-level data containment, factuality-adjusted model rankings, and model-specific orchestration above open agent protocols.

title: The Six-Month Signal — Kimi K3 narrows the open-model cost gap
description: Kimi K3 moves a frontier-cost forecast, Lila Sciences turns experiments into training data, and OpenAI reframes AI buying around cost per successful task.

title: The Six-Month Signal — The Answer Key Became an Attack Surface
description: A public-safe editorial brief on OpenAI's Hugging Face evaluation security incident, Gemini 3.6 Flash task economics, customer-service latency tradeoffs, and METR's expenditure horizon for automated research.

title: The Six-Month Signal — Stripe's Kai, Routed AI Economics, and Chai-2
description: Stripe's 5,000-user internal agent rollout, the split economics of routed coding and production voice AI, and Chai Discovery's lab-measured antibody-design claim.

title: The Six-Month Signal — Claude Code's Auto Mode Default, Cloudflare's Agent Browser, and the Routing Margin
description: Anthropic's 1,053-tester study behind Friday's auto-mode default, Cloudflare's agent-built Kitesurf browser and stateless MCP, Cursor Router's 68% cost cut at above-frontier satisfaction, OpenAI's gated GPT-5.6-Cyber, and Flo Crivello in his own words on AI-employee economics.

title: Meta's Open-Weights Return, and OpenAI's Margin Defense
description: Muse Glimmer brings Meta back to open weights under Apache 2.0 — a 30B agent-tuned model that runs on one GPU — but the agentic benchmark trails the marketing. OpenAI's agent SDKs quietly default to the cheapest model tier, ads come to ChatGPT, and a Chinese VC explains why Anthropic's and OpenAI's ARR numbers are not measured the same way.

title: The Six-Month Signal — 2026-08-12: Encrypted reasoning traces decoded; NVIDIA ships the agent execution layer
description: A research team shows the encrypted chain-of-thought blobs returned by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google can be replayed, decoded, and ported — 62 API keys and 33 passwords recovered from ~7,000 public traces. NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning plus Switchyard routing put hard numbers on the two-tier agent stack (LangChain: 7% of turns need a frontier model; 74% cheaper at ~93% accuracy). An unreleased Claude lifts a 150-year-old Riemann bound to 67.2% with a machine-checkable proof. AISI reports Mythos 5 deception in testing; OpenAI discloses colluding test agents. Clip: The Circuit on AMD's unforecasted CPU demand.

title: Grok 4.6 at Eighty-Four Cents a Task; DeepSeek's Sunday Repricing; the RSI Yardstick
description: The Six-Month Signal for Thursday, August 13, 2026: SpaceXAI's Grok 4.6 reaches the frontier at a measured eighty-four cents per task; DeepSeek moves to peak and off-peak billing on August 16; NVIDIA research VP Ming-Yu Liu on why model capabilities converge; and twenty-five frontier researchers on recursive self-improvement.

title: The Six-Month Signal — GLM-5.3: post-training is all they did
description: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 matches Kimi K3 at a third of the size with post-training alone, and the open weights land in two weeks — the show's named cost-board tripwire. DiG-bench measures whether models can discover hidden rules (frontier models clear a fifth of the hardest tier; humans sweep it). Qwen 3.8 27B is excellent on a laptop but ships a token-burning reasoning default. Quick hits: business AI usage splits (8.3x token gap; best-model share flat at 6%), Dario Amodei concedes the delivery gap, 404 Media AirTags Amazon's book-scanning facility, and The Circuit stress-tests Nvidia's $500B financing bet — with a 22-second clip.

title: The Six-Month Signal — Tuesday, August 18, 2026
description: Stripe all but closes a $7B purchase of OpenRouter — $140M annualized revenue, 70% gross margins, 250 trillion tokens a month, and the public rankings tape that comes with it. Cursor's Origin starts hosting code inside the SpaceX fold. And Rich Sutton tells Sequoia why models that never stop learning are the real prize — in his own words.

title: The Model You Can't Have, the Memory You Can't Afford
description: Anthropic's August Risk Report reveals an internal model ahead of its public frontier, scoring 62.8% on substituting for its own researchers. Memory prices hit 2007 levels as hyperscalers lock in 2027 DRAM supply, and the AI buildout starts crowding out Treasurys. OpenAI halves flagship prices on OpenRouter while a laptop-sized Qwen ties Luna. Plus: a 17-year-old reaches ICML's main track on an eight-hundred-dollar budget.

title: The Context Pipe Did
description: The same model jumps from 33 to 75 with a better search API; AT&T publishes a 56% routing-cost cut; Generalist shows one-shot physical learning; and OpenAI previews private safety processing.

title: Headway Builds the Agent It Couldn't Buy
description: Headway's disposable-container agent, Mistral's retrieval-loop benchmarks, Apple Messages permissions, Linear's runtime pricing, and a Coding Agent Index version break.

title: Agent traffic gets a real benchmark
description: SemiAnalysis opens AgentX, a multi-turn inference benchmark built around long-context coding-agent traffic. METR finds discovery acceleration is sharp in cyber but absent from public optimization trend lines, while Simile AI makes the case for validated human-behavior simulation. The episode includes a 21-second clip from Simile cofounder Joon Sung Park.

title: Jalapeño and the Harder Scoreboard for Agents
description: OpenAI's first inference chip meets its missing workload test; voice agents split on charm versus completion; and Parallel rebuilds web search for machine customers.

title: Astra's Quiet Reasoning Test
description: OpenAI's Astra crosses a critical cyber threshold as visible reasoning may shrink; Anthropic moves safeguards into customer-controlled cloud infrastructure; and Glean claims a large context-and-routing task-cost gap.

title: Meta's fifty-five-cent frontier, Anthropic's quiet pause, and the AOL theory of model companies
description: Muse Spark 1.3 ties GPT-5.6 Sol on intelligence at fifty-five cents a task — the cheapest at the frontier tier — moving the show's cost board from 52 to 60. Anthropic discloses eval incidents and a weeks-long RL pause. Plus: Zeng Ming on why model companies are the next AOL, Fable 5.1's token bill, Gemini 3.8 Flash, and Muse Voice Transcribe.

title: Astra Clears the Capability Bar, Not the Cost Rule
description: ARC Prize verifies a step-change in GPT-6 Astra while a cost-cap conflict keeps the forecast open; plus OpenAI agents coordinating through public wikis, Snowflake's enterprise-agent adoption denominator, and Nvidia's Hugging Face deal.
